execution_paths: login obtains a GitHub device code, opens the provider verification URI, polls the OAuth token endpoint and stores credentials with mode 0600.
The token authorizes dashboard.captive.dev requests; the returned cluster endpoint becomes the kubeconfig.
kubectl, pg_dump, pg_restore and shell sessions run through explicit user commands. Restore drops the selected app schema before restoring the supplied dump.
UpdateChecker fetches a version manifest and prints an update instruction; it does not execute a fetched program.
samples.context_missing: No deployment context; the reviewed operations match the declared platform-administration purpose.

execution_paths: Shell.Plugin.Run takes host, port and shared key from its caller; ClientSocket receives framed bytes, decrypts with AES/ECB using an MD5-derived key, then Messages.Read dispatches R/, runshell and closeshell.
R/ starts a hidden CMD.EXE with redirected stdin/stdout/stderr; runshell writes the supplied input; output callbacks encrypt and send the output over the same socket.
Keylogger installs a global low-level keyboard hook, records printable and bracketed special keys plus foreground titles, and sends the resulting GetKeylogger records over the encrypted socket.
Options.RunOptions dispatches WDDisable to hidden PowerShell Set-MpPreference commands that disable multiple Defender protections.
Options.BSOD enables privilege 19 then calls NtRaiseHardError with status 0xc0000022 and shutdown response 6.

HVNC.Plugin.Run passes its embedded DLLBuffer image and caller-supplied endpoint arguments to RunPE.PERun targeting Framework/v4.0.30319/cvtres.exe. HandleRun creates a suspended host, unmaps its image, writes replacement headers and sections, replaces the thread context and resumes it.
samples.obfuscation: ILSpy recovered the managed control paths. Module helpers extract native Protect*.dll support libraries from CLR resources and resolve exported delegates. HVNC builds API names from byte arrays. Resource extraction, socket AES decryption and CMD tasking are independent paths, refuting the former encrypted-resource-command-stager claim.
samples.context_missing: The archive has plugins and supporting libraries rather than a deployed configured implant. Endpoints and keys are caller supplied. This limits attribution and victim identification, but does not remove the malicious shell, surveillance, security-disable and crash capabilities.

execution_paths: Decoded the MSI string pool and column-major tables: ProductName=AteraAgent, Manufacturer=Atera networks, cabinet member=AteraAgent.exe.
CustomActions install the Microsoft .NET runtime, initialize account-scoped settings, and manage the AteraAgent service. Account and installation identifiers are configured in the MSI.
Parsed the .NET 6-format single-file bundle and extracted Atera.Agent.Windows.dll and Atera.Agent.dll for ILSpy decompilation.
Program.Main selects Windows service or CLI hosting; the service is named AteraAgent.

The agent connects to vendor APIs and certificate-authenticated MQTT for enrollment and commands. ReceivedCommandsHandler.Validate verifies the command signature before parsing and executing it. CommandSignatureVerifier uses RSA/SHA-256.
PE Authenticode identity reports Atera Networks Ltd with an intact digest. The apphost inherits OriginalFilename Atera.Agent.Windows.dll while shipping as AteraAgent.exe.
samples.context_missing: The outer zoominstaller.msi name is concerning but collector controlled. No download page, deployment authorization, account ownership or executed operator task is available. The account-scoped stock RMM behavior does not establish an unauthorized installation.

trait_changes.reason: Consolidate duplicate Open3 capture observations in the subprocess mechanism. Tighten text matches to actual Open3 receiver calls. Explicit references updated; shell-directory selectors intentionally no longer receive non-shell Open3 calls.
An arbitrary variable named bun or BUN_EXE does not establish Bun identity; generic capture still records process creation.
An OR of generic capture/popen calls and subshell syntax does not establish shell execution on every passing branch. Canonical process observations remain.
Independent resource, reflection, crypto and process references do not bind resource bytes to activation or establish an attack. Neutral constituent traits remain.
Require an executable OriginalFilename to infer a renamed vendor executable; DLL version stamps on native managed-app hosts do not establish this claim.
Signer subject is notable provenance; it neither convicts RMM nor proves product identity.
Recognize equivalent shell-task and keyboard-hook spellings and require buffered keylog context plus either a named keylog record or bracketed special-key records.

The production OneOffSpec Kubernetes manifest builder is not a test. A suffix alone establishes a naming property; retain explicit consumers but remove this observation from broad testing-directory selectors.

Combine equivalent test/spec source suffix observations across JavaScript, TypeScript and Ruby in one naming trait. Both exact former JavaScript consumers were audited: AsyncFunction is JavaScript/TypeScript scoped; the archive hook also retains its JavaScript/ZIP scopes. Ruby consumers retain their Ruby scopes except the generic HTTP source-context group, where this intentionally also recognizes JavaScript test/spec suffixes. No new directory or budget exception.
